ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

rockwood — pattern 5

A high-energy shoulder injury causes marked superior clavicular displacement. Coracoclavicular distance is approximately 180% greater than the opposite side, and the deltotrapezial soft-tissue envelope is extensively disrupted. There is no posterior displacement on the axillary view. Which Rockwood acromioclavicular injury type best fits this pattern?

  1. Type VI
  2. Type I
  3. Type II
  4. Type III
  5. Type V
Answer and explanation

Type V

Type V: Marked superior displacement with extensive deltotrapezial disruption and a coracoclavicular distance increase greater than 100%.

Option explanations

Type V: Type V: Marked superior displacement with extensive deltotrapezial disruption and a coracoclavicular distance increase greater than 100%.

Type VI: Type VI describes inferior displacement of the distal clavicle, beneath the acromion or coracoid. The case instead matches Type V.

Type I: Type I describes an AC ligament sprain with intact coracoclavicular ligaments and no radiographic displacement. The case instead matches Type V.

Type II: Type II describes aC ligament disruption with coracoclavicular ligament sprain and mild displacement. The case instead matches Type V.

Type III: Type III describes complete AC and CC ligament disruption with superior displacement and a coracoclavicular distance increase of about 25–100%. The case instead matches Type V.
